content.title: About
content.content: Salmon sushi is a classic Japanese dish consisting of vinegared rice topped with a slice of fresh salmon. The fish adds a buttery flavor, vibrant color, and a boost of omega‑3 fatty acids.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sushi originated in Southeast Asia as a method of preserving fish in rice.
Salmon in sushi can be served raw (sashimi‑style) or lightly seared (aburi).
Traditional sushi rice is short‑grain and has a lower starch content than regular rice, giving the rolls a sticky texture.
In Japan, “nigiri” refers to a hand‑pressed oval of rice topped with a slice of fish.
Salmon sushi gained worldwide popularity due to its balanced taste and versatility.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Salmon provides EPA and DHA, omega‑3 fatty acids that support heart and brain health.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Each piece delivers complete amino acids essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Salmon is a good source of vitamin B12 and niacin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The dish supplies selenium, phosphorus and potassium, which aid immunity and bone health.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with red meat, salmon contains less saturated fat, making it heart‑friendly.

items.title: Food‑borne infection risk
items.content: Raw salmon may harbor parasites and bacteria; use fish that has been frozen or sourced from reputable suppliers.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to seafood and may react to salmon.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Soy sauce and seasoned rice can increase sodium intake, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: While the pieces are small, added sauces or mayo can raise the calorie count of a serving.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sushi is typically served with soy sauce, wasabi and pickled ginger. Dip the piece lightly in soy sauce, add a dab of wasabi if desired, and enjoy each bite in succession.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep prepared sushi refrigerated, covered with plastic wrap, and consume within 24 hours. For longer storage, freezing is possible, though the rice texture may change.
